text:
maria: Observed a p99 tail jump after yesterday's kernel selection tweak. First-token latency for streaming requests climbed ~35ms on p95 and ~120ms on p99 for long-context chats. Not sure if it's batching or the new kernel fallback.
ajay: Can you paste the canary config + perf snapshot? Any change to microbatch size or flush interval?
sam: fwiw, kernel selector started preferring kernel_v2 for mixed-length seqs at the 2.3 rollout. Might increase kernel switch overhead on cold KV hits.
maria: here's the relevant snippet from the deploy: 
```
kernel_selector:
  policy: latency_weighted
  prefer: [kernel_v2, kernel_v1]
microbatch:
  target_tokens: 64
  max_wait_ms: 25
streaming:
  chunk_tokens: 32
  flush_ms: 80
kv_cache:
  ttl_ms: 60000
  on_miss: fetch_sync
```
leo: Hmm, chunk_tokens=32 + flush_ms=80 seems high for perceived latency. First token won't hit until either chunk fills or flush timeout. That's likely hurting time_to_first_token.
tess: We care about both throughput and perceived latency. Reducing chunk to 8 or 16 might help p95 without killing throughput if batching adjusts.
ajay: Agree. Also microbatch target of 64 may create batch_fill_time if requests are small. What are our batch fill latencies?
maria: Telemetry over the hour of the incident: 
- time_to_first_token p50=40ms p95=210ms p99=420ms
- batch_fill_latency p50=7ms p95=90ms p99=200ms
- kv_hit_rate ~ 78%
- kernels_selection_switches per_min increased x3 during the spike
ci-bot: CI note: perf-regression-alert #483 triggered at 1818889123, linked report https://perf.redwood/internal/483
sam: If kernel switches are frequent, we might pay context/transform overhead when switching execution path. Two hypotheses: 1) streaming flush waits for chunk_tokens; 2) batch fill latency amplified by microbatch target and our scheduling quantum.
maria: Quick A/B idea: roll a canary with chunk_tokens=12, flush_ms=40, microbatch.target_tokens=32 on 5% traffic, observe time_to_first_token and overall throughput.
leo: Also instrument a metric: time_to_first_kernel_exec and kernel_switch_count per request. Might catch the switching cost.
ajay: I'll add a short profiler trace around the kernel selection + kv lookup path (50ms sampling) and add to the canary.
sam: Also try forcing kernel_v1 for a subset to see if p99 improves — isolates selector overhead.
tess: Product note: customers noticed "sluggish first word" on demo yesterday. We should prioritize perceived latency fixes for hosted tier.
maria: Action items:
- @ajay add profiler + canary config (chunk 12/flush 40, microbatch 32) -> roll to 5% (by EOD)
- @sam run kernel_v1-only canary to compare
- @leo add metrics: kernel_switch_count, time_to_first_kernel_exec
- @tess coordinate notes for support and update status page if canary shows improvement
- I'll monitor p95/p99 and post summaries here.
ajay: on it, will link the canary config and TRACES here when ready.
sam: I'll prepare the kernel_v1 canary and a small synthetic load that matches PLG spinner traffic.
leo: I'll add the metrics + dashboard tiles (time_to_first_token, kernel_switches, kv_hit_rate) and set alerts p99>400ms.
maria: Thanks. If anyone sees regression in throughput, revert canary and we'll try flush_ms=20 + chunk_tokens=16 next. :thumbsup:

maria: I'll post a short follow-up once we have 30m of canary data.
